To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
feature dependencies can be classified into four kinds, and they can be used to model the requirements and the solution space of the software.

(i) requirements dependencies are not only important for requirements analysis and specification but also for software architecture and design; (ii) the feature-orientation provides an effective approach to analyze and manage requirements dependencies; (iii) feature dependencies can be classified into static feature dependencies, dynamic feature dependencies, and specification level feature dependencies; (iv) there are connections and interrelationships between these three kinds of feature dependencies.

feature-oriented modeling of requirements dependencies is a promising way for software developers and requirements analysts to better understand the requirements and to improve the software development process.
